ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ is $8$, and $\angle ACB=60^\circ$, then what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OA and OB, and draw OH $\perp$ AB at H, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ACB=$60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOB=$2\angle$ACB=$120^\circ$, \\
$\because$ OB=OA=8, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOH=$\angle$BOH=$60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAB=$30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ OH=$\frac{1}{2}$OA=4, \\
$\therefore$ AH=$\sqrt{OA^{2}-OH^{2}}=\sqrt{8^{2}-4^{2}}=4\sqrt{3}$, \\
$\therefore$ AB=2AH=$\boxed{8\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the image shows triangle ABC inscribed in a circle, with A and B on the lower part of the circle and C on the upper right; O is marked as the circle center, so the given circle is the circumcircle of triangle ABC. From the text, read that the circumradius is R=8 and the inscribed angle ∠ACB is 60°. Since side AB is opposite ∠C in triangle ABC, apply the extended law of sines: AB/sin(∠ACB)=2R. Therefore AB=2·8·sin60°=16·(√3/2)=8√3.
